skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Creates isolated Git worktrees for feature work, including directory selection, ignore checks, setup commands, and baseline test verification.
skill.summary: Create isolated Git worktrees with safety checks before starting implementation work.
skill.author: Cycleaddict

security_audit.summary: The static backtick, hidden-path, and /dev/null findings are false positives caused by Markdown documentation and legitimate worktree paths. The main risks are semantic: the skill directs agents to run package manager and test commands automatically, and it can commit .gitignore changes without explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: Automatic package and test commands can execute repository-controlled code.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running install, build, or test commands, especially in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to commit .gitignore changes without asking.
remediation.suggestion: Change the workflow to propose the .gitignore edit and request confirmation before committing any repository change.

remediation.issue: The global worktree path under ~/.config may surprise users.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the exact target path and ask for confirmation before creating directories outside the repository.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Project Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the agent to automatically run dependency installation and test commands such as npm install, cargo build, pip install, poetry install, npm test, pytest, and go test. These commands can execute project-defined code in untrusted repositories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicitly listed and the prose says to auto-detect and run setup before verifying tests. Package managers and test commands commonly execute repository-controlled scripts.

semantic_findings.title: Unconfirmed Repository Commit Instruction
semantic_findings.description: When a project-local worktree directory is not ignored, the skill instructs the agent to add a .gitignore entry, commit the change, and proceed. This can alter repository history without explicit user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction to commit is direct and unconditional after ignore verification fails. The risk is workflow integrity rather than covert exfiltration, so confidence is high but severity is moderate.

content.value_statement: Feature work can disrupt an active checkout and make baseline state unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through isolated Git worktree setup with safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Selects an existing .worktrees or worktrees directory when present.
Checks CLAUDE.md for a stated worktree directory preference.
Verifies project-local worktree directories are ignored by Git.
Creates a new worktree and branch for isolated feature work.
Runs detected project setup and baseline test commands.
Reports the final worktree path and test status.
limitations: Requires a Git repository with worktree support.
Can run package manager and test commands that execute project code.
Does not choose a branch name unless the user or task supplies one.
May need user input when no worktree directory preference exists.

use_cases.title: Start Feature Development
use_cases.description: Create a clean worktree before implementing a feature while preserving the current checkout.

use_cases.title: Prepare Parallel Fixes
use_cases.description: Set up separate branches for unrelated fixes without switching the active workspace.

use_cases.title: Validate Baseline State
use_cases.description: Install project dependencies and run tests before starting implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a named branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a Git worktree for branch feature/login and tell me the final path.

prompt_templates.title: Use Project Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up an isolated worktree for this task. Follow the repository worktree directory preference if one exists.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Before Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a clean baseline before coding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for the payment refactor, install detected dependencies, run baseline tests, and report any failures before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Control Risky Commands
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use in an unfamiliar repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a worktree for feature/search, but ask before running install, build, test, or commit commands.

output_examples.output: The assistant checks the preferred directory, verifies it is ignored, creates the branch worktree, and reports the ready path.

output_examples.input: Set up a worktree and verify the baseline.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates the isolated workspace, runs detected setup and tests, then reports pass or failure status before implementation.
The assistant asks whether to use a project-local hidden directory or a global configuration directory.

best_practices: Confirm the branch name and worktree location before creating files.
Ask before running install, build, test, or commit commands in unfamiliar repositories.
Review baseline test failures before starting implementation work.
anti_patterns: Creating a project-local worktree without checking Git ignore rules.
Running dependency installation in an untrusted repository without confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a separate Git worktree and branch for isolated development work.

faq.question: Does it change my current checkout?
faq.answer: It is designed to avoid disrupting the current checkout by using a separate worktree.

faq.question: Why does it check .gitignore?
faq.answer: It checks ignore rules to avoid accidentally tracking nested worktree contents.

faq.question: Can it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow can run install, build, and test commands after creating the worktree.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Ask for confirmation before running package manager or test commands in untrusted code.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
